summary: Resample and warp the spatial dimensions
description:
Resamples the spatial dimensions (x,y) of the data cube to a specified resolution and/or warps the data cube to the target projection. At least `resolution` or `projection` must be specified.

Related processes:

* Use ``filter_bbox()`` to set the target spatial extent.
* To spatially align two data cubes with each other (e.g. for merging), better use the process ``resample_cube_spatial()``.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Resamples the data cube to the target resolution, which can be specified either as separate values for x and y or as a single value for both axes. Specified in the units of the target projection. When the resolution is `0` (the default), additional up- and down-sampling is minimized on a best-effort basis.

schema.description: A single number used as the resolution for both x and y.
A two-element array to specify separate resolutions for x (first element) and y (second element).

parameters.name: projection
parameters.description: Warps the data cube to the target projection, specified as [EPSG code](https://spatialreference.org/ref/epsg/) or [WKT2 CRS string](http://docs.opengeospatial.org/is/18-010r7/18-010r7.html). By default (`null`), the projection is not changed.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description:
Resampling method to use. The following options are available and are meant to align with [`gdalwarp`](https://gdal.org/programs/gdalwarp.html#cmdoption-gdalwarp-r):

* `average`: average (mean) resampling, computes the weighted average of all valid pixels that the target pixel covers at least partly. Each pixel is weighted by the fraction of it that the target pixel covers.
* `bilinear`: bilinear resampling.
* `cubic`: cubic resampling.
* `cubicspline`: cubic spline resampling.
* `lanczos`: Lanczos windowed sinc resampling.
* `max`: maximum resampling, selects the maximum value from all valid pixels that the target pixel covers at least partly.
* `med`: median resampling, selects the median value of all valid pixels that the target pixel covers at least partly. The values are not interpolated: for an even number of values, the smaller of the two middle values is selected.
* `min`: minimum resampling, selects the minimum value from all valid pixels that the target pixel covers at least partly.
* `mode`: mode resampling, selects the value which appears most often among all valid pixels that the target pixel covers at least partly, with each pixel weighted as for `average`. In the case of ties, the first value identified as the mode is selected.
* `near`: nearest neighbour resampling (default), selects the pixel that contains the center of the target pixel. A center exactly on the border between pixels belongs to the pixel that starts at the border (the right one horizontally, the lower one vertically).
* `q1`: first quartile resampling, selects the first quartile value of all valid pixels that the target pixel covers at least partly. The values are not interpolated: of the `n` sorted values, the value at the (one-based) position `ceil(0.25 * n)` is selected.
* `q3`: third quartile resampling, selects the third quartile value of all valid pixels that the target pixel covers at least partly. The values are not interpolated: of the `n` sorted values, the value at the (one-based) position `ceil(0.75 * n)` is selected.
* `rms`: root mean square (quadratic mean) of all valid pixels that the target pixel covers at least partly, weighted as for `average`.
* `sum`: computes the weighted sum of all valid pixels that the target pixel covers at least partly, weighted as for `average`, so that the total is preserved.

Valid pixels are determined based on the function ``is_valid()``. A target pixel that covers no valid pixel is set to the no-data value.

parameters.name: align
parameters.description: Specifies to which corner of the spatial extent the new resampled data is aligned to.

returns.description: A raster data cube with values warped onto the new projection. It has the same dimensions and the same dimension properties (name, type, labels, reference system and resolution) for all non-spatial or vertical spatial dimensions. For the horizontal spatial dimensions the name and type remain unchanged, but reference system, labels and resolution may change depending on the given parameters.
